title: Lessons from Building an ESP32 Edge Platform for Solar and EV Telemetry
excerpt: Moving from a single-purpose inverter monitor (Flin V1) to FlinEdge, a 7-phase architecture for solar, battery and EV hardware.
author: Manoranjan Das
bodyHtml:
Flin V1 was a proof of concept: an ESP32 talking RS232 to a Voltronic PI30 inverter, pushing readings somewhere useful. It worked, but it was one device, one protocol, one job.

Generalizing the edge platform

FlinEdge starts from a different question: what does a reusable edge platform for solar, battery and EV hardware need to support, not just one inverter model. That means a pluggable protocol layer, a consistent telemetry schema regardless of the underlying hardware, and an architecture split into seven phases so each layer — transport, protocol adapters, storage, sync, and control — can be built and tested independently.

What carries over from V1

The RS232/PI30 experience from Flin V1 directly informed FlinEdge's protocol adapter design: timing quirks, checksum handling and reconnect behavior that only show up after running against real hardware for weeks, not minutes.

Proof-of-concept firmware earns its keep by surfacing exactly these problems before they're baked into a platform meant to outlast any single inverter model.
